method: Three passes as requested. Each pass builds on the previous one; the findings below are the real defects/gaps found and what was done.

pass_1_implement_and_verify.scope: Review repo; reproduce and explain the portal error; restore data autonomously; run the pre-registered designed factorial; study why 0.2477 won; rank and validate hypotheses; build verified downloads, executive guide, site, registries, feed and CI.
done: Reviewed the old GEMSDOE25 tree and the owner's sibling repos (GEMSDOE24 evidence); found the invented-footprint file (IR-25-NAN-FOOTPRINT/-OVER-EMISSION/-FAKE-PIPELINE/-DTI-KERNEL).

Data placement solved: scripts/restore_data.py restores 419 MB raster + labels + template + external layers from the owner's public repos with SHA-256 pins (end-to-end run from an empty directory: 20 s).
Pre-registered (04, 05) then executed 2^(5-1) Resolution V factorial (16 runs x 8 cells, 31 min) and add-on / emission tests; confirmation replicate with fresh draws.
Forensics of the scored rasters: 0.2477 file == dot_thin(H19-5, 1.5) pixel-for-pixel; lattice and live pair give |G| 12.5k / 12.8k; out-of-sample check on the H25/H28 pair.
Strict writer/checker reproduces the portal-accepted 0.2477 file's pixels and raster profile; primary file is byte-identical (SHA-256) to the group's unscored alternate.
Site (root index.html + 3 sub-pages), README with the verbatim brief, AGENTS.md, AI_DISCLOSURE.md, registries, ToS-compliant feed script + workflows.

found_and_fixed: ruff found an f-string with nested same-type quotes that is a SyntaxError on Python 3.11 (this sandbox's version) in scripts/build_site.py: fixed (twice, the second time in code added later).
A claim of 'Spearman 1.000' between the training tc band and GeoDAWN TC was a rounding of 0.9999: corrected in registry and docstring.

'byte-for-byte' was used where only mask equality had been verified: reworded to 'pixel-for-pixel', then 'byte-identical' used only after the full SHA-256 of the re-written D2.8 file matched the group's file.
The verbatim brief file had abbreviated the second (identical) copy of the results list: restored in full so the README copy really is verbatim.

Executive page showed an informational check ('strict whole-array check fails for any NaN') as a red FAIL, mislabelled the zeros fallback as 'NaN outside', and implied a declared exception was needed although the gate passed: all fixed, plus provenance wording ('pinned organizer grid' -> expected grid/footprint of the owner's mirror).
File name said d2-4 while note and site said D2.8 (same pixel set): renamed to d2-8 to match the group's naming.
Preview server initially served the whole repo including .git: restarted on a site-only directory.
Plain requests cannot reach api.github.com from the sandbox: feed script falls back to the authenticated gh CLI so the committed seed feed is real data.
Old broken TIFs were still in docs/downloads: removed, with a regression test that they are neither shipped nor linked.
Experiments are deterministic: two logged cells re-run from scratch reproduced DTI to 1e-9.
Hidden-components design checked for leakage (collar, whole-component hiding, visible-only catalogue features, labels never used for GDR points) and covered by tests.
known_residual_risks: Hide-and-recover is a catalogue-gap proxy; the harness scores the H19 family ~2.7x lower than live while reproducing the blind lattice within ~5 % (IR-25-PROXY-LIMITS).
Family E very likely flatters the proxy; the +ALL add-on gain is weakly supported (t = 1.97, 3 d.f.).
The dotting model's out-of-sample error is -0.017, larger than the predicted +0.008 gain of D2.8 over D1.5.

pass_3_recheck_against_the_original_brie.method: Re-read the brief line by line (README, 'Owner brief (verbatim)') and mapped each requirement to an artefact.

mapping.easy one-click TIF, obvious at the start: index.html hero card; README download box; docs/executive-summary.html
mapping.fix 'Predicted values must be in range [: root cause + fix + reproduction test (evidence/old_gems25_tif_forensics.json, src/gems25/submission.py, tests/test_submission.py)
mapping.unique name and short note: content-addressed file name and a <=120-character note per file (registry/submissions.json)
mapping.rank which families matter alone / in co: frozen classification rule applied mechanically (E, B alone; none in combination; A, C, D inert)
mapping.why/how 0.2477 and can we beat it; leade: evidence/why_0_2477.json, evidence/emission_model*.json, knowledge/07, site Research page
mapping.3-5 untried hypotheses with layers, sign: knowledge/03 (+ addendum with outcomes); H26-4 obtainability checked (not downloadable here)
mapping.line-by-line verification from official: registry/sources.json (20 sources, verification status), registry/irregularities.json (20 items), docs/sources.html
mapping.deep research stored for other projects;: knowledge/06 digest and section 4 'overlooked or under-used sources'
mapping.data-placement blocker: scripts/restore_data.py (SHA-256 pinned), verified end to end
mapping.multiple passes; PR and merge: this file; the PR is opened from the fixed session branch into main and its status is reported in the PR and the final message (not asserted in this file)

gaps_found_and_closed: Dropbox links in the brief: one share page was opened (name only); the rest unreachable -> recorded as unverified with exact wording, not claimed.
GeoDAWN licence line absent from the page text read -> flagged IR-25-LICENSE-GEODAWN instead of repeating 'CC0'.
Terms-of-Use scope (also bars manual monitoring without consent) -> flagged IR-25-TOU for the owner.

checks: CI (pytest + ruff) green on the PR head and on main after the merge
GitHub Pages build for main reported 'built'; the public root page and the executive-summary page were fetched and show the new site
the three shipped GeoTIFFs stored on main were hashed via the GitHub API and match registry/submissions.json exactly
the source-feed workflow ran on main, contacted only non-DrivenData hosts and skipped the 8 DrivenData sources by policy
not_verified: the TIF bytes as served by the Pages edge (github.io is unreachable from the sandbox shell)
